lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Capacity, Mass and Volume
lesson.summary: Measure how much a container holds and how heavy things are, using litres, millilitres, grams and kilograms.
learning_objectives: Read scales and choose the right unit

standards.text: Choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure mass (kg/g) and capacity (litres/ml) to the nearest appropriate unit, using scales and measuring vessels; compare and order

success_criteria: I can say how much a container holds in litres or millilitres
I can say how heavy something is in grams or kilograms
I can read a scale and choose a sensible unit
lesson.real_life: Pouring lemonade, buying a bag of rice at the shop, or baking with Aunty Noor.

warm_up.prompt: A feather is lighter than a brick.
warm_up.hint: Which one would you lift easily?

blocks.alt: A clear glass measuring cup with millilitre marks up its side
blocks.caption: A measuring cup with marks for millilitres.
blocks.credit: Photo by Steve A Johnson on Unsplash
blocks.say: Meet Zara. She helps Aunty Noor in the kitchen. They pour, they weigh and they bake. Look at this measuring cup. Today we measure how much things hold.

blocks.markdown:
**Capacity** is how much a container can hold.

**Volume** is how much is inside it now.
blocks.say: A jug can hold water. How much it can hold is its capacity. How much water is in it now is its volume.

scenes.caption: Capacity: 1 litre.
scenes.say: Here is an empty jug. It can hold one litre. That is its capacity.

scenes.caption: Volume: half a litre.
scenes.say: Pour in some water. The jug is half full.

scenes.caption: Capacity same, volume changes.
scenes.say: The capacity stays the same. Only the volume changes!

question.prompt: Which word means how much a jug can hold?
question.hint: It is the most it can hold.
question.explanation: Capacity is how much a container can hold.

blocks.markdown:
A **litre** is about a big carton of juice.

A **millilitre** is a tiny amount, about a drop. 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
blocks.say: We measure capacity in litres. A big juice carton holds one litre. A tiny drop is one millilitre. One litre is one thousand millilitres.

scenes.caption: 1 litre.
scenes.say: A big carton holds one litre. It is for drinks.

scenes.caption: A spoon: millilitres.
scenes.say: A spoon holds a few millilitres. That is for medicine.

scenes.caption: 500 ml + 500 ml = 1 litre.
scenes.say: Half a litre is five hundred millilitres.

blocks.alt: A measuring jug marked from 0 to 1 litre with the 500 ml mark labelled and the water at 700 ml
blocks.caption: The water is at 700 ml.
blocks.say: Look at this jug. It goes up to one litre. Half way is five hundred millilitres. The water is at seven hundred.

blocks.title: The tall jug and the wide jug
blocks.transcript: Baker Imran has a small shop. Today he makes milk bread. First he weighs the flour. One kilogram is one thousand grams. The heavier side goes down. When they match, it is just right. Now the milk. Imran has a tall jug and a wide jug. Which one holds more? It looks like the tall one! Imran pours the tall jug into the wide jug. It fits exactly! Both jugs hold one litre. Shape can fool our eyes. Always measure. Shukriya, Imran!
blocks.caption: A baker finds out the tall jug does not hold more.

points: Capacity: the most it can hold
Volume: how much is in it now
blocks.say: Remember. Capacity is what it can hold. Volume is what is in it. Litres for big, millilitres for small.

terms.meaning: How much a container can hold.
How much is inside it now.
A tiny unit for liquid. 1000 make a litre.
Something that holds things, like a jug.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Pour a cup into a jug

blocks.markdown:
To **compare** is to see which is more or less.

4 cups of 250 ml fill a 1 litre jug.
blocks.say: Zara fills a cup. She pours it into a jug. How many cups fill the jug? Let's count the pours.

scenes.caption: 1 cup = 250 ml.
scenes.say: One cup holds two hundred and fifty millilitres.

scenes.caption: 4 cups.
scenes.say: Pour one, two, three, four cups. The jug is full!

scenes.caption: 4 × 250 ml = 1000 ml.
scenes.say: Four cups make one litre. Now we can compare!

blocks.title: Pour the juice
blocks.goal: Fill 1 litre of juice into the jug by moving 10 little cups. Move all of them into the jug.

question.prompt: A jug holds 1 litre. A glass holds 100 millilitres. How many glasses fill the jug?

blocks.markdown:
To **estimate** is to make a sensible guess.

Then measure to check your estimate.
blocks.say: Before you pour, guess. A guess is an estimate. Then pour and check. A tall jug is not always bigger. Always check!

blocks.title: A tall jug and a wide jug

scenes.caption: Two jugs.
scenes.say: One jug is tall and thin. One is short and wide.

scenes.caption: Same capacity.
scenes.say: Pour water from the tall one into the wide one. It fits exactly!

scenes.caption: Both = 1 litre.
scenes.say: Both hold one litre. A tall shape can fool your eyes!

blocks.title: Pour at home
instructions: Guess how many cups fill the jug.
Pour one cup at a time and count.
Try a different jug and compare.

question.prompt: Which holds more: 1 litre or 750 millilitres?

blocks.say: Remember. Pour and count. Estimate first. Do not trust a tall shape.

terms.meaning: To see which is more or less.
To tip a liquid from one container to another.
A container with a handle for liquids.

mini_quiz.explanation: You estimate first and measure after.

blocks.markdown:
**Mass** is how heavy something is.

On a **balance**, the heavier side goes down.
blocks.say: Now we weigh things. How heavy something is, is its mass. A balance has two pans. The heavier side goes down.

scenes.caption: Mango and grape.
scenes.say: A mango on one side. A grape on the other.

scenes.caption: Mango is heavier.
scenes.say: The mango side goes down. It is heavier!

scenes.caption: Grape is lighter.
scenes.say: The grape side goes up. It is lighter.

blocks.alt: Balance scales with a rice bag in one pan and a 1 kg weight in the other, the rice side tipping down because it is heavier
blocks.caption: The heavier side goes down.
blocks.say: Look at these scales. The rice bag is in one pan. A one kilogram weight is in the other. The heavier side goes down.

question.prompt: On a balance, which side goes down?

blocks.markdown:
A **gram** is tiny, about a raisin.

A **kilogram** is big, about a bunch of bananas. 1 kg = 1000 g.
blocks.say: We measure mass in grams and kilograms. A raisin is about one gram. A bunch of bananas is about one kilogram. One kilogram is one thousand grams.

scenes.caption: About 1 gram.
scenes.say: A raisin is one gram. A paper clip is one gram too.

scenes.caption: 1 kilogram.
scenes.say: A bag of rice is one kilogram. It is much heavier!

scenes.caption: 1000 g = 1 kg.
scenes.say: One thousand grams make one kilogram.

blocks.title: Kitchen match
blocks.say: Flip the cards and find the matching pairs. A little brain break!

question.prompt: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?

points: Grams are small, kilograms are big
blocks.say: Remember. Mass is how heavy. Grams are small. Kilograms are big. Big things are not always heavy.

terms.meaning: A big unit of mass. 1000 grams.
A tool with numbers to read.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which unit is best for a bag of rice?
mini_quiz.explanation: A bag of rice is measured in kilograms.

blocks.markdown:
A **scale** has numbers to read.

Read where the needle or water stops.
blocks.say: At the shop in Lahore, Zara buys a bag of rice. It says five kilograms. The needle on the scale shows how heavy it is.

scenes.caption: 0 to 10 kg.
scenes.say: The scale goes from zero to ten kilograms.

scenes.caption: Halfway = 5.
scenes.say: The needle is halfway. Halfway between zero and ten is five.

scenes.caption: 5 kg of rice.
scenes.say: The rice is five kilograms. Read the needle, not the bag!

question.prompt: Zara buys 2 kg of rice and 3 kg of flour. How many kilograms in all?

blocks.markdown:
**Altogether** means add the amounts.

250 ml + 750 ml = 1000 ml, or 1 litre.
blocks.say: Aunty Noor makes lemonade. She uses two hundred and fifty millilitres of lemon juice. She adds seven hundred and fifty millilitres of water.

scenes.caption: 250 ml.
scenes.say: Pour in the lemon juice. Two hundred fifty millilitres.

scenes.caption: + 750 ml.
scenes.say: Now add water. Seven hundred fifty millilitres.

scenes.caption: 1000 ml = 1 litre.
scenes.say: That makes one thousand millilitres. A full litre jug!

blocks.prompt: Which is heavier: a kilogram of feathers or a kilogram of rice? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: They are the same. Both are one kilogram. The feathers just take up more space.

question.prompt: A jug has 600 millilitres of water. Zara adds 400 millilitres. How many millilitres now?

points: Add amounts with the same unit
Pick the right unit for the job
blocks.say: Remember. Read the scale where the needle stops. Add amounts with the same unit. Choose a sensible container.
